skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render MP4 videos from React and Remotion TSX components through the inference.sh CLI. Configure resolution, FPS, duration, codec, props, and common Remotion APIs.
skill.summary: Generate MP4 videos from Remotion React components using inference.sh.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples. The real risks are the broad infsh CLI allowlist, remote rendering of user-provided code, and a remote image reference.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the specific render command pattern or require user confirmation for non-render infsh actions.
Add a clear warning that TSX code, props, and assets are sent to inference.sh and should not contain secrets.
Replace the hosted image with a local or marketplace-hosted asset to avoid third-party image requests.

static_findings.snippet: > Requires inference.sh CLI (`infsh`). Get installation instructions: `npx skills add inference-sh/s
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable way to turn React animation code into finished video files. This skill runs Remotion component code through inference.sh and returns MP4 renders.
actual_capabilities: Runs the inference.sh Remotion render app from TSX component input.
Supports common Remotion imports including AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, and interpolate.
Accepts render settings for width, height, FPS, duration, codec, and props.
Provides CLI examples for fade text, counters, spring animation, and sequences.
Shows Python SDK usage for normal runs and streaming progress updates.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, an account login, and network access.
Sends component code and props to an external rendering service.
Does not provide local Remotion rendering or offline video generation.
Render success depends on valid TSX and supported Remotion or React APIs.

use_cases.title: Generate Product Videos
use_cases.description: Create branded MP4 clips from reusable React components and product data.

use_cases.title: Automate Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render animated titles, counters, and sequences without manual video editing.

use_cases.title: Render Data-Driven Updates
use_cases.description: Turn changing data and props into repeatable social or reporting videos.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner render from an existing component idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short Remotion component with a fade-in title and render it as a 1080p MP4.

prompt_templates.title: Add Props to a Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate render with reusable text inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a Remotion video that accepts title and subtitle props for a three second announcement clip.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sequenced Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion composition with three timed text sections, spring motion, and a 30 FPS render.

prompt_templates.title: Stream a Long Render
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python SDK pattern to render a ten second Remotion video and report progress until the MP4 is ready.

output_examples.input: A request for a two second fade-in welcome animation at 1920 by 1080.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares the Remotion component, runs the render command, and returns the generated MP4 location.

output_examples.input: A request for a square loading counter video with smooth progress animation.
output_examples.output: The assistant renders a 1080 by 1080 video with a percentage counter and clear completion details.

output_examples.input: A request to monitor a longer render from Python.
output_examples.output: The assistant uses streaming progress updates and reports the final video location when rendering completes.

best_practices: Keep TSX components small, deterministic, and focused on one composition.
Review props and component code before sending them to inference.sh.
Set explicit width, height, FPS, and duration for repeatable output.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, tokens, or private source code in render inputs.
Do not rely on unsupported browser APIs inside the Remotion component.
Do not use very large assets without checking render time and service limits.

faq.question: Does this skill render videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI to run the Remotion render app remotely.

faq.question: What input format does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects TSX code that exports a default React component for Remotion rendering.

faq.question: Can I pass custom props?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented input accepts a props object for component values.

faq.question: Which video settings can I control?
faq.answer: You can set width, height, FPS, duration in seconds, composition ID, and codec.

faq.question: Is network access required?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires inference.sh login and remote rendering through its CLI or SDK.

faq.question: Should I send confidential code?
faq.answer: No. Treat render inputs as data sent to an external service unless your organization approves it.
